newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Oct 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
STALKERS TO FACE FIVE-YEAR JAIL TERMS

Tough new measures have been introduced by the Home Office today to deter stalkers. A combination of criminal and civil measures, with unlimited fines, are being introduced in order to curb stalking and harassment.
BANKS TO SELL OFF 80 MILLION STG OF EUROTUNNEL DEBT
Since Eurotunnel's refinancing deal deal was announced last week, approximately 80 million stg of the company's bank debt has been sold on to other investors.
JAPAN TRADE CHEER FOR THE GREENBACK
The announcement of a 30 percent fall in Japan's trade surplus kept the dollar above 112 yen in Asian trading.
LUCASVARITY PONDERS ON A NEW IMAGE

The new chief executive of LucasVarity, Victor Rice, has commissioned outside consultants to advise on whether the company should change its name and corporate image to improve the recently merged group's profile in the U.S. and Europe.
VIRGIN SET TO CREATE A STIR WITH PERSONAL PENSION OFFER

Today Richard Branson's makes his boldest move yet in the financial services market, by launching a low-cost British index-tracking personal pension. The product is likely to attract criticism from traditional life insurance and pensions companies and independent financial advisers.
